stem.text: The function f is defined on the closed interval \( [-2, 5] \) and is twice differentiable at every x in that interval except \( x = 1 \), where f has a jump discontinuity. Also \( f'(2) = 0 \) and \( f''(2) > 0 \). Must f attain an absolute minimum value on the closed interval \( [-2, 5] \)? Justify the answer.

answer_key.label: No, because f is not continuous on the closed interval \( [-2, 5] \), so the Extreme Value Theorem does not apply.

worked_solution.text: f has a jump discontinuity at \( x = 1 \), inside the interval, so f is not continuous on \( [-2, 5] \).
A hypothesis of the Extreme Value Theorem fails, so the theorem gives no conclusion and f need not attain an absolute minimum value.

options.label: Yes, because f is defined at every x in the closed interval \( [-2, 5] \), so the Extreme Value Theorem applies.
